note: Alternating tetrapod, the spider's walk: legs I and III on one side step with II and IV on the other, then the other four, so four feet are always down. Each set is staggered a little from front to back, which is the metachronal ripple a real spider shows and which keeps eight identical footfalls from reading as two. The stride is short against the wheelbase because a spider's wheelbase is its leg SPAN, not its body -- 10cm of step on a 50cm span. Head pitch is a touch positive so the face stays level while the thorax dips, and the abdomen lifts a little off the bind pose and sways with the stride. The bind pose holds legs I, II and IV at full stretch, so `legHold` draws their stance stations in toward the body -- the front pair back, the back pair forward -- to give the stride somewhere to go; leg III stands sideways and its step is a swing at the hip, not a reach.
